title: Domain name disputes - how cybersquatting cases actually get resolved
p1:
Someone registers a domain name that looks exactly like your brand. Can they really keep it forever?

Many people assume the first person to buy a domain owns the right to use it. That is not always true.
p2: A surprising fact: trademark owners can sometimes recover a domain even if someone else registered it first. This often happens in cybersquatting cases, where a person registers a domain mainly to profit from another brand’s reputation.
p3:
The resolution usually happens through a process called UDRP (Uniform Domain-Name Dispute-Resolution Policy). A complaint is reviewed by an independent panel, which looks at factors like trademark rights, bad-faith registration, and whether the domain owner has a legitimate reason to use the name.

If the complaint succeeds, the domain can be transferred to the rightful party. The key lesson for businesses: protecting your brand online is not only about owning a domain, but also monitoring how your name is being used.
conclusion: Have you ever seen a domain name that looked like it was copying a real brand? What action do you think should be taken?
